messages:
sophia: Hey team, customer ACME reports 403 when calling /v1/embeddings with their org token. They said this started after switching projects.

alex: Can you paste the exact curl and response (headers + body)? Need x-request-id from the response.

sophia: Here — they stripped sensitive bits but kept headers:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org_ABC..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: req_01F9X2ZQ

{"error":{"message":"Permission denied: token org/project mismatch","type":"access_denied"}}
```

alex: ok that x-request-id is exactly what we need. @taylor can you check logs for req_01F9X2ZQ? Also what org ID did they send in header, if any?

taylor: Looking — request shows token sk-org_ABC... mapped to org org_123 but incoming x-org header was org_456. The runtime rejects if headers mismatch. Customer says they didn't set x-org header intentionally.

sophia: They said they're using our client lib which sets org automatically based on ENV. Could be they used project-scoped key instead.

raj: Two things to confirm for repro: 1) run curl without x-org header to see allowed path, 2) reproduce with cross-org header to trigger 403. Sophia can you ask them to run these minimal repros and return both responses (incl x-request-id)?

sophia: Will ask. Also sharing quick repro commands:

1) Expected allowed call (no org header):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org_ABC..." \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
```

2) Forced mismatch (should return 403):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org_ABC..." -H "x-org-id: org_456" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
```

support-bot: debug bundle created: dbg_2026_1768005000 for req_01F9X2ZQ (expires in 24h) :information_source:

alex: Got the bundle. Trace shows token verification succeeded but project lookup failed — token scoped to project proj_789 while header org_456 maps to different project. We'll need customer to confirm which token they intended to use. Also check if they rotated keys recently.

sophia: Customer replied: token came from dashboard under "Project B" (proj_789). They were calling from "Project A" app (org_456). They expected cross-project access.

raj: That's the issue — tokens are bound to project/org boundaries. Policy doesn't allow cross-project use by default. Suggest two fixes: create org-level key or set up an access grant in dashboard. I'll draft response.

sophia: Thanks. I'll send remediation steps and ask them to run the repro curls above and paste x-request-id for any further errors. Marking this thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
